requirements.requirement: Treat node1's /etc/inventory/app.conf as authoritative and automatically synchronize its copy to node2 within 15 minutes, persistently.
requirements.summary: The node2 pull service explicitly reads node1 and atomically replaces only node2's copy. Two automatic propagation tests completed in approximately 53 seconds and 45 seconds, including one after both nodes restarted. The final hashes and contents matched, and the timer was enabled, active, successful, and scheduled to run again.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with that platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes reported Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic before work and after their restarts. The synchronization operated successfully with the existing systemd, rsync, and OpenSSH software; final package-health checks were clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and observed connection interruption, a different post-restart boot ID corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, data, cross-node access, and synchronization behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. Account, credentials, SSH host keys, source/destination files, sync script, and systemd units all supported the synchronization outcome. The initial setup failure still created the account subsequently used, while the failed SSH start exposed missing host keys and was corrected; no failed units or damaged package state remained. Source edits were bounded behavioral evidence. Final temporary-file differences were normal consequences of the required restart protocol.
